**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blocker. This is a `feat`: it merges at the next cut.

Review tier: SAFETY. The PR changes posted G-code (the LN2W program under `G41` / `G42`). First review of this PR. Ownership record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4246#issuecomment-7205671801

## What looks good

- The moves stay the wire-centre path. The kerf, threading and slug laws judge the same moves as before. `a_die_square_is_programmed_on_its_profile_under_g41` pins that the moves do not change.
- The domain code is in the motion crate (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/comp.rs`). The app file `operation/wire_comp.rs` holds the command door and the glue only.
- Each refusal has a name. `comp.rs` has no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` outside the tests.
- The door refusal is in `wire_gate`, which `create.rs` and `edit.rs` call. The generator asks the same refusal again for a loaded file.
- A post without `onRadiusCompensation` (Generic ISO Wire) is refused by the engine. `g-edm.cps` and `sodick-wire.cps` refuse the offset by name.
- The project key and the stamp do not move for `computer`. No tracked golden is in the diff.
- The body has `Process change: yes`, a `Changelog:` line, "Goldens moved" and `Fixes #4134`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. The decision record is `docs/decisions/4134-wire-control-offset.md`.
- The new test file joins the directory suite `wire_post/`. It makes no new test binary.
- The diff has no UI change (one test literal in `crates/ui`). Screenshots are not necessary. Issue #4243 owns the UI control.

## Goldens, read line by line

`edm_test_square_offset.nc`:

- `C001` comes before `G41 H001`. `C002` comes before `G41 H002`. `C903` comes before `G41 H003`.
- Each pass programs `X5. Y0.`, then the four corners at `X±5. Y±5.`, then `X5. Y0.`. The walk is counter-clockwise. The wire is on the left, inside the die: `G41` is correct.
- Each pass ends with `G40 G01 X0. Y0.`. The lead-in is 5 mm, which is more than each offset.
- The comments state 0.165, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. These are the wire radius 0.125 mm plus the gaps 0.040, 0.020 and 0.010 mm.

`edm_test_2axis_offset.nc`: I calculated the centre and the two end radii of each arc from its I and J words.

| Arc centre | Programmed radius | Part radius |
|---|---|---|
| X-13. Y-3. (three arcs) | 2.500 | 2.5 |
| X-21. Y-3. (two arcs) | 3.000 | 3 |
| X-6. Y-3. (two arcs) | 2.000 | 2 |

The start and end radii of each arc agree to 0.001 mm. The slot edges are at `Y-2.8` and `Y-3.2`. The program ends with `G40 G01 X-13. Y-3.`, `T90`, `M02`.

## Mutations

I ran each mutation in the review worktree and then restored the file. The tree is clean again.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `comp.rs`, `pass_side`: the offset side inverted (`== die` to `!= die`) | RED: 7 of the 9 `wire_edm::comp::tests` |
| `wire_comp.rs`, `apply`: each skim gets the radius of the rough pass | RED: `the_ln2w_square_posts_the_part_contour_with_the_controls_offset` (golden) |
| `gates.rs`: the door refusal off | RED: `the_offset_with_a_taper_or_an_open_run_is_refused_at_the_door` |
| `params/cutting.rs:53`: the stamp does not digest the mode | GREEN: no test fails (follow-up 1) |

Probes (temporary local tests, removed, not in the PR):

- An L-shaped profile, die and punch, forward and reversed, with `sharp_corners` on. Each programmed ring is on the profile. The side is correct for each direction.
- A reversed skim gets `G42`, and it programs the same profile.
- A punch whose start hole is nearest to a corner of the wire path: see note 2.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Follow-ups (file after merge)

1. **P7, a missing test.** No test pins that the stamp digests the mode (`crates/app/src/operation/params/cutting.rs:53`). The mutation above stays green in `app lib`, `wire_stamp`, `stock_stamp`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour`, `project_roundtrip` and `mcp_wire_contour`. Add a test to `crates/app/tests/wire_stamp.rs`: the stamp of `control` and of `wear` is different from the stamp of `computer`, and they are different from each other. Without the digest, an edit of the mode can keep a cached path of the other mode.
2. **P7, a missing test.** Only the Mark 21 refusal has an app test (`crates/app/tests/wire_post/sodick_aq600l_offset.rs:80`). Add the same pin for `Generic ISO Wire EDM` and for `G-EDM` with a Wire Contour in `control` mode.
3. **P7, a missing golden.** Control mode on a drawn DXF chain has no pin (the body says so). `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_cut.rs:110` can walk the wire path at the offset plus a margin. The programmed contour is then the profile plus that margin. The control cuts the judged wire path, so the cut is correct. But the comment `THE PATH IS THE PART CONTOUR` is then correct only to that margin.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/comp.rs:34` says "the 1 um lattice". `cl::lattice` rounds to 1e-6 mm, which is 1 nm. The value `1e-5` agrees with "ten lattice steps". Only the unit in the comment is wrong.
2. When the seam is at a corner of the wire path, the engage block ends one offset before the part corner, on the line of the first edge. The cancel block starts one offset after it, on the line of the last edge. My probe gave `X-5.165 Y-5.` and `X-5. Y-5.165` for a punch square with the start hole at `X-12. Y-12.`. With the register at the stated radius, the control cuts the judged wire path. The decision record says this ("Refusing a seam at a corner"). No test pins it.
3. `crates/app/src/operation/wire_comp.rs`: its `use` lines name none of the five (world, project file, command, MCP, CLI). I accept it: the file reads the app types `WireContourOp` and `WireCondition`, and it holds the refusal of the command door. The domain code is in the motion crate.
4. `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (+4 lines), `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs` (+1), `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs` (+1) and `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs` (a comment) were more than 400 lines before this PR.
5. The span builder uses the radii that the caller gives. A wrong radius moves the programmed contour off the part. The app gives the radii of the same conditions that the generator uses, and the square golden pins this for the three passes (mutation 2).
6. The LN2W words are not verified on a control. The program header says so.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
